clue.text: Tour guide takes company on a bender with little hesitation

parts.note: Uri Geller, the showman famous for bending spoons, is a bender
er is the short sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: A tour leader goes on a drinking spree with the firm, barely pausing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On a bender' suggests a drinking binge; it is really Uri Geller, the spoon-bender, giving URI.
explanation.definitionFit: A courier is a travel representative who escorts and looks after tourists on a trip.

clue.text: Athlete runs round first of laps -he grinds out a living

indicators.note: the athlete's letters run round, enclosing the next piece

parts.note: a miler is an athlete who races over a mile

indicators.note: first of means take the opening letter of laps

explanation.surface: A runner circles the track after the first lap, and is described as a man working hard for his wage.
explanation.definitionFit: A miller works a mill grinding grain into flour, earning his keep by grinding.

clue.text: Fool with lots more old money to start with gets slap on the mouth

indicators.note: to start with places the swap at the opening letter of the fool word

parts.note: a dipstick is slang for a stupid person
in old British money L (pound) is worth far more than D (penny)

explanation.surface: An idiot with extra cash gets smacked in the face.
explanation.walkthrough: In pre-decimal British money, D was a penny and L a pound; replacing the first letter D with L swaps in 'lots more old money'. 'Slap' is slang for make-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Slap is British slang for cosmetics, and the colour applied to the lips is a cosmetic for the mouth.

clue.text: Male -he's crestfallen to get engaged

indicators.note: crestfallen means the top letter of he's falls to the bottom of the word

explanation.surface: A man is downcast at becoming betrothed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crestfallen' moves the H, the crest of HES, to the end, making ESH.
explanation.definitionFit: Gears that mesh interlock, and engaged gears are interlocked.

clue.text: Bit of lamb God set up in approved way

indicators.note: in a down entry set up means the word for God is written upwards, reversed

parts.note: Allah is the Arabic name of God

indicators.note: bit of means just the first letter of lamb

explanation.surface: A portion of lamb prepared according to divine rules.
explanation.definitionFit: Hallal (halal) describes meat slaughtered as Islamic law permits, so prepared in a sanctioned manner.

clue.text: Money invested in a mine in California

indicators.note: in here means the mine sits inside the abbreviation for the state

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine

explanation.surface: Funds put into a gold mine in California.
explanation.definitionFit: Capital is the money put into a business as its investment base.

clue.text: One group of detectives probing domestic murder

indicators.note: probing means pushing into, so these letters go inside the domestic word

parts.note: home is an adjective meaning domestic, as in home affairs
I is the Roman numeral one
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police

explanation.surface: A detective squad investigates a killing in the home.
explanation.definitionFit: Homicide is the legal term for one person killing another.

clue.text: An enthusiast securing good heroin — like this?

definitions.text: An enthusiast securing good heroin — like this?

indicators.note: securing means holding inside, so the fan word encloses the two letters

parts.note: a fan is an enthusiast
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: A drug fan scores quality heroin, asking if it comes from a certain country.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is wordplay and definition: heroin from Afghanistan is famously plentiful.
explanation.definitionFit: Much of the world's heroin comes from Afghanistan, so a user getting it would get the Afghan kind.

clue.text: Tear in limb upset monster

indicators.note: in means the tear word goes inside the reversed limb
in a down clue upset turns the limb word upside down, reversing it

parts.note: a leg is a limb
to rend is to tear

explanation.surface: A rip in a leg upsets a fearsome beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Limb' tempts the solver toward arm; only the leg reading works when turned upside down in a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Grendel is the man-eating creature slain by Beowulf in the Old English epic.

clue.text: Car turns over

explanation.surface: A motor vehicle flips.
explanation.definitionFit: A Rolls is a Rolls-Royce automobile; to roll is to rotate over, so it turns over.

clue.text: Swiss handle most credit

parts.note: a helve is the handle of an axe or tool

indicators.note: most means drop the final letter of the credit word

parts.note: tick is British slang for credit, as in buying on tick

explanation.surface: Switzerland takes charge of most of the lending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On tick' is British slang for on credit.
explanation.definitionFit: Helvetic comes from Helvetia, the Latin name for Switzerland.

clue.text: Young racehorse, one highly bred, in acceleration yards ahead

indicators.note: ahead puts the yards letter at the front of the other pieces

parts.note: Y is the abbreviation for yards
an earl is a nobleman, one of high birth
g is the symbol for acceleration due to gravity

explanation.surface: A colt with a noble pedigree speeds up and pulls yards in front.
explanation.definitionFit: A yearling is a horse in its second year, the age of young racehorses sold at auction.

clue.text: Old actress in costume getting Oscar

parts.note: garb is clothing or costume
Oscar is the radio alphabet code word for O

explanation.surface: A veteran star in period dress wins an Academy Award.
explanation.walkthrough: Greta Garbo was a Swedish-born Hollywood star of the 1920s and 1930s.
explanation.definitionFit: Greta Garbo was a film star of the past, so an actress of old.

clue.text: Dressed lady in authentic mode

indicators.note: dressed means arranged or prepared, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman dressed in genuine fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: In church music, an authentic mode has its final as its lowest note, unlike a plagal mode.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lydian is one of the medieval church modes classed as authentic rather than plagal.

clue.text: Several bilk ill-treated prospective murder victim

indicators.note: ill-treated means badly handled, so the letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A number of swindlers cheat a man marked for death.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Henry Baskerville is the heir targeted for death in Conan Doyle's The Hound of the Baskervilles.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Sherlock Holmes novel, Sir Henry is the intended target of a killing plot.

clue.text: Raver is spoiling shows

indicators.note: spoiling means ruining, so the letters are wrecked and rearranged

explanation.surface: A partygoer is ruining the performances.
explanation.definitionFit: To show up is to turn up, so shows means comes or gets there.

clue.text: Italian team against Arsenal losing heart by half-time

parts.note: Inter Milan is an Italian football club
V is short for versus, against

indicators.note: losing heart means removing all the middle letters of Arsenal, leaving its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A Milan side playing Arsenal are flagging by the break.
explanation.walkthrough: Arsenal is a London football club; Inter is Inter Milan.
explanation.definitionFit: The interval is the break in a match, which comes at half-time.

clue.text: Jailer born in foreign country

indicators.note: in means the born letter goes inside the country

parts.note: Turkey is a country abroad
N is an abbreviation for born (natus)

explanation.surface: A prison guard was born abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: A turnkey is an old word for a prison warder who keeps the keys.

clue.text: E.g. McCartney -one of Beatles on Help

indicators.note: one of picks a single letter, the initial, from Beatles

parts.note: to assist is to help

explanation.surface: Paul McCartney, a Beatle, sang on the album Help!
explanation.definitionFit: Paul McCartney played bass guitar in the band, an example of a bass player.

clue.text: In grip of liquor umpire has minimum competence for decisions

indicators.note: in grip of means the letters are held within the words liquor umpire

explanation.surface: A drunk umpire barely has the ability to make rulings.
explanation.definitionFit: A meeting needs a minimum number present before it is competent to take binding votes.

clue.text: Soldier, one in First World War battle

indicators.note: in means the one letter goes inside the battle

parts.note: the Marne was the site of two major battles in 1914 and 1918
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A soldier fighting in a battle of the Great War.
explanation.definitionFit: A marine is a soldier serving with a naval force.

clue.text: Lacking one of 25 in working order, being non-essential

indicators.note: lacking means the working word is without the letters of one epoch

parts.note: operational means working properly
25-down's answer is a plural meaning times, so one of them is a single age or epoch

explanation.surface: A machine missing a part but still working proves to be unnecessary.
explanation.definitionFit: Something optional is a matter of choice, not compulsory.

clue.text: Choose one degree giving best results

parts.note: to opt is to choose
I is the Roman numeral one
MA, Master of Arts, is a university degree

explanation.surface: Pick a qualification that leads to top outcomes.
explanation.definitionFit: Optima is the plural of optimum, the most favourable outcome.

clue.text: All there is in revues providing diversion

indicators.note: diversion here means turning aside, so the letters are redirected into a new order

explanation.surface: Variety shows offer everything one might want for entertainment.
explanation.definitionFit: The universe is the whole of existence, everything that exists.

clue.text: Times? One of several alternatives here

definitions.text: Times? One of several alternatives here

parts.words: Times? One of several alternatives here
parts.note: the word for ages can be rearranged into several other words, such as ears, sear and rase, so this spelling is one option among them

explanation.surface: A newspaper offers one of a number of choices.
explanation.definitionFit: Eras are ages or periods of time.

clue.text: Bull is used in Indian food

parts.note: bull is slang for nonsense, as is rot

explanation.surface: Beef is an ingredient in a curry dish.
explanation.definitionFit: A roti is a round unleavened flatbread eaten in South Asia.

clue.text: Familiar racing driver, such an ass mostly going round

indicators.note: going round means the shortened donkey word encloses the next piece
mostly means drop the last letter of the donkey word

parts.note: a jenny is a female donkey
so can mean such, as in 'so great' for 'such greatness'

explanation.surface: A well-known Formula One star behaves like a fool going round the track.
explanation.walkthrough: Familiar signals a first name: Jenson Button, the British Formula One world champion.
explanation.definitionFit: Jenson Button is a British racing driver, known familiarly by his first name.

clue.text: Top celebrities concealing weapon spreading fear

indicators.note: concealing means hiding inside, so the celebrity word wraps the weapon

parts.note: the A-list is the top tier of celebrities
an arm is a weapon

explanation.surface: Famous stars hide a gun, causing panic.
explanation.definitionFit: An alarmist causes needless panic by exaggerating dangers.
